In [[geometry]], the '''Nagel point''' (named for [[Christian Heinrich von Nagel]]) is a [[triangle center]], one of the points associated with a given [[triangle]] whose definition does not depend on the placement or scale of the triangle. It is the point of [[Concurrent lines|concurrency]] of all three of the triangle's [[Splitter (geometry)|splitters]].

==Construction==
Given a triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}, let {{mvar|T{{sub|A}}, T{{sub|B}}, T{{sub|C}}}} be the [[extouch triangle|extouch points]] in which the {{mvar|A}}-[[excircle]] meets line {{mvar|BC}}, the {{mvar|B}}-excircle meets line {{mvar|CA}}, and the {{mvar|C}}-excircle meets line {{mvar|AB}}, respectively.  The lines {{mvar|AT{{sub|A}}, BT{{sub|B}}, CT{{sub|C}}}} [[concurrent lines|concur]] in the Nagel point {{mvar|N}} of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.

Another construction of the point {{mvar|T{{sub|A}}}} is to start at {{mvar|A}} and trace around triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} [[semiperimeter|half its perimeter]], and similarly for {{mvar|T{{sub|B}}}} and {{mvar|T{{sub|C}}}}. Because of this construction, the Nagel point is sometimes also called the '''bisected perimeter point''', and the segments {{mvar|{{overline|AT}}{{sub|A}}, {{overline|BT}}{{sub|B}}, {{overline|CT}}{{sub|C}}}} are called the triangle's [[Splitter (geometry)|splitters]].

There exists an easy construction of the Nagel point.  Starting from each vertex of a triangle, it suffices to  carry twice the length of the opposite edge. We obtain three lines which concur at the Nagel point.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Elementary construction of the Nagel point|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-02558108|last=Dussau|first=Xavier|date=April 2020|website=HAL|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

<br />
[[File:Easynagel.gif|center|thumb|485x485px|Easy construction of the Nagel point]]

== Relation to other triangle centers ==
The Nagel point is the [[isotomic conjugate]] of the [[Gergonne point]]. The Nagel point, the [[centroid]], and the [[incenter]] are [[collinear]] on a line called the ''Nagel line''. The incenter is the Nagel point of the [[medial triangle]];<ref name="Anonymous">{{cite journal
 | author = Anonymous
 | title = Problem 73
 | department = Problems for Solution: Geometry
 | journal = [[American Mathematical Monthly]]
 | volume = 3
 | issue = 12
 | pages = 329
 | year = 1896
 | doi = 10.2307/2970994
 | jstor = 2970994}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://polymathematics.typepad.com/polymath/why-is-the-incenter-the-nagel-point-of-the-medial-triangle.html|title=Why is the Incenter the Nagel Point of the Medial Triangle?|website=Polymathematics}}</ref> equivalently, the Nagel point is the incenter of the [[anticomplementary triangle]]. The [[Mixtilinear incircles of a triangle|isogonal conjugate of the Nagel point]] is the point of concurrency of the lines joining the mixtilinear touchpoint and the opposite vertex. 

== Barycentric coordinates ==
The un-normalized [[Barycentric coordinate system|barycentric coordinates]] of the Nagel point are <math> (s-a:s-b:s-c) </math> where <math>s = \tfrac{a+b+c}{2}</math> is the semi-perimeter of the reference triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.

== Trilinear coordinates ==
The [[trilinear coordinates]] of the Nagel point are<ref name="Gallatly">{{cite book
 | author = Gallatly, William
 | title = The Modern Geometry of the Triangle
 | edition = 2nd
 | year = 1913
 | pages = 20
 | publisher = Hodgson
 | location = London}}
</ref> as

:<math>\csc^2\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)\,:\,\csc^2\left(\frac{B}{2}\right)\,:\,\csc^2\left(\frac{C}{2}\right)</math>

or, equivalently, in terms of the side lengths <math>a=\left|\overline{BC}\right|, b=\left|\overline{CA}\right|, c=\left|\overline{AB}\right|,</math>

:<math>\frac{b + c - a}{a}\,:\,\frac{c + a - b}{b}\,:\,\frac{a + b - c}{c}.</math>

==History==
The Nagel point is named after [[Christian Heinrich von Nagel]], a nineteenth-century German mathematician, who wrote about it in 1836.
Early contributions to the study of this point were also made by [[August Leopold Crelle]] and [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | author = Baptist, Peter
 | title = Historische Anmerkungen zu Gergonne- und Nagel-Punkt
 | journal = Sudhoffs Archiv für Geschichte der Medizin und der Naturwissenschaften
 | volume = 71
 | year = 1987
 | issue = 2
 | pages = 230–233
 | mr = 0936136 }}</ref>
